summary:
Habitable Earth is a project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, with the aim of finding places on Earth that can help us better understand the environments of the Moon and Mars. The project focuses on identifying locations that share certain environmental and geographical characteristics with potential sites for future permanent human settlements beyond Earth.

Through an interactive globe, users can explore different parts of our planet, search for locations, and discover possible Earth analogs. The idea is to connect places we already know with environments that we are still trying to understand. These locations can serve as valuable starting points for research, experimentation, and studying some of the challenges that future astronauts may face.

We believe that preparing for life beyond Earth should begin with understanding our own planet. Habitable Earth brings this idea into an accessible and interactive experience, helping people see how Earth's diverse environments could contribute to the future of space exploration and humanity's journey towards living on the Moon and Mars.
details:
Project Details – Habitable Earth

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Habitable Earth is an interactive web application developed to identify locations on Earth that share environmental and geographical similarities with potential settlement regions on the Moon and Mars.

Through an interactive globe, users can explore different locations, search for places, and discover potential analog environments. The idea is to make it easier to understand how studying certain places on Earth can help us prepare for the challenges of future human settlements beyond our planet.

2. What benefits does the project have?

The application makes planetary analog research easier to explore and understand. It can help students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts discover Earth locations that may be useful for studying extraterrestrial environments. It also encourages Earth-based research and experimentation, connecting what we know about our planet with what we hope to learn about the Moon and Mars.

3. What is the intended impact the project?

Our aim is to make the search for Earth-based analog locations more accessible and useful for future space exploration. Studying these environments can help us better understand certain challenges astronauts may face when establishing permanent settlements on the Moon and Mars. We also hope to encourage more people, especially students, to take an interest in planetary science and space research.

4. What tools and coding languages were used?

The application was developed using:

  • HTML: For the structure and content.
  • GitHub: For source code management.
  • GitHub Pages: For hosting and publishing the application.

It can be accessed through a web browser without requiring any specialized hardware.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative idea behind Habitable Earth is to look at our planet from the perspective of future space exploration. Instead of treating Earth and other celestial bodies as completely separate subjects, we connect their environments through an interactive geographical experience.
